what: To produce `git diff <ref> -- <path>` for an untracked file you just wrote in a worktree, run `git add -N <path>` first (intent-to-add). Without it, git treats the working-tree file as if it doesn't exist relative to index and reports the ref's version as a pure deletion instead of a modification diff.
why: Hit this while producing rebrand diffs: scope files existed on feature/phase-1 but not in my worktree's HEAD, so `git diff feature/phase-1 -- path` showed the file being "deleted" until I ran `git add -N`. This is the standard way to get review-ready unified diffs when your branch doesn't track the files yet.
